text:
SRE Bot: INCIDENT detected — elevated p99/p95 latency for streaming and increased tail stalls across cross-zone flows in eu-west-2 and us-east-1. Auto-triggered alert group: stream-tail-latency, net-queueing. Severity: P1.
Aisha: I'm on it. current impact: several customers report stalled streaming responses and timeouts on websocket sessions. seeing p99 jump from ~1.2s to 6–8s. p95 up to ~2.3s.
Jon: grabbing traces. initial observation: spike correlates with cross-zone NAT egress queues in eu-west-2b -> nat-gw-42. Packet retransmits and TLS handshake retries visible.
Priya: confirmed — Cloud metrics show nat-gw-42 ephemeral port exhaustion spike at 2134567700 UTC. conntrack table growth on the NAT instance around same time.
Aisha: ok, tag network + infra. @Dan can you join?
Dan: here. I'm seeing TLS SYN retransmits and +30% TCP retransmit rate on the inter-AZ path. Flow logs show bursts of long-lived connections being re-established rather than reused — looks like session affinity failures causing midstream reconnects into other AZs.
Jon: stack traces from runtime show streaming layers retrying when partial frames drop; KV cache hits are fine. this feels network path related, not model runtime.
Priya: support queue has 4 customers reporting disconnected streams and elevated latencies. CS: high business impact for one paying customer (ingestion pipeline).
Aisha: mitigation plan proposal: 1) divert new egress from nat-gw-42 to nat-gw-45 in same region (prefer AZ-local nat-gw where possible). 2) flush conntrack on nat-gw-42 and increase ephemeral port allocation temporarily. 3) throttle long-lived cross-zone re-establishs at proxy layer for 10m to reduce conntrack churn. 4) put auto-fallback to regional non-cross-zone routing for streaming route.
Dan: I can add a route policy to bias toward AZ-local nat-gw. pushing change now to route-table-azb-2 to prefer nat-gw-45 for subnets with streaming traffic. doing it in a canary: azb only.
SRE Bot: Deploy/Change request recorded: change_id=chg-2134567890-azb-route. Owner=Dan.
Jon: rolling a lightweight proxy change to cap reconnection bursts: adding 150ms jitter and 2s backoff for immediate reconnects. patch pushed to canary in azb.
Priya: support notified customers, created incident ticket INC-2134567 and attached problem summary.
Aisha: executing conntrack flush on nat-gw-42 — running `sudo conntrack -F` now (will be disruptive for existing ephemeral flows). doing in maintenance window style: 1 AZ at a time.
Dan: conntrack flush done on nat-gw-42. ephemeral port allocation increased from 1024-61000 to 15000-61000 on the edge.
Jon: observing initial drop in retransmits; p99 dropping from 8s -> 3.1s across azb, but still elevated in azc.
Dan: pushing same route bias to azc now to favor nat-gw-47.
SRE Bot: Route change chg-2134567890-azc applied by Dan.
Aisha: monitoring telemetry. p95 back to ~1.4s in azb, p99 ~2.8s. azc still ~4.5s p99. We'll keep the flow.
Priya: CS reports one customer resumed streams after reconnect. others still flaky but improved.
Lukas: I'll prep a fallback plan: if latency doesn't normalize to p99 < 2s in 15m, we shift streaming traffic to regional peering path (non-cross-zone) and open a maintenance notice.
Jon: adding packet captures for postmortem: `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/azc_stalls.pcap port 443 and tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn) != 0` capturing TLS handshake retries.
Aisha: for scope: affected services = streaming-api (edge), ws-proxy, router layer; models unaffected. Root cause hypothesis: conntrack/nephemeral-port exhaustion on specific NAT gateways amplifying TLS handshake tail latency and causing streaming stalls due to reconnect churn.
Dan: temporary config note: increasing NAT ephemeral lower bound reduced collisions; conntrack flush cleared stuck states. Longer-term: autoscale nat-gw instances on conntrack high-water mark and implement ephemeral port range expansion by default.
Priya: customer impact log updated. Severity remains P1 until p99 < 2s across all AZs and no active reconnects.
SRE Bot: PagerDuty events cleared for azb after metrics recovered below threshold.
Jon: azc still needs one more cycle; I'm seeing a small rate of client reconnects due to lb stickiness mis-route. investigating affinity tokens.
Aisha: permission to roll a rollback of last LB stickiness patch? it was deployed ~1h before spike.
Dan: go for rollback if it reduces cross-AZ affinity misses. I'm prepping the revert.
SRE Bot: Change recorded chg-2134567890-lb-rollback. Owner=Jon.
Jon: rolled back LB stickiness change to previous hashing. Rolling restart of 2/3 routers in azc to pick up config.
Priya: customers in azc reporting improvement. p99 in azc trending down 4.5s -> 1.9s over last 6 minutes.
Aisha: good. marking mitigations: 1) conntrack flush + ephemeral port bump (done), 2) route bias to AZ-local nat-gw (done), 3) proxy reconnect jitter/backoff (deployed canary, will roll), 4) LB stickiness rollback (done).
Lukas: I'm taking on-call watch for the next 2 hours. summary for handoff: incident 2134567890, root cause hypothesis conntrack/ephemeral exhaustion on nat-gw causing handshake retransmits & streaming reconnect churn, mitigations applied (conntrack flush, ephemeral range bump, route bias, lb rollback, proxy jitter). Current status: p99 ~1.6–2.0s region-wide; customer reports improving.
Aisha: thanks @Lukas. I'll add post-incident action items: schedule nat autoscale, add alert on ephemeral port usage, review LB stickiness rollout checklist.
Support Bot: Notified impacted customers with status updates and expected next update in 30m.
Lukas: will keep monitoring and escalate if regressions. closing active paging. If anyone sees re-escalation, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
